text:
maya: quick heads-up — running a 6h saturation sim overnight and we see a persistent token "leak" after GKE preemptions. TPM peaks fine but sustained throughput drops by ~8%.

pranav: do you mean tokens consumed without matched responses (kv cache lost, retries)?

maya: yup. pattern: eviction -> reconnects -> small number of inflight requests get retried and double-counted in the ledger.

sasha: that matches some logs I saw friday. redis-sync lag spikes 200-500ms, and our reconciler currently only runs every 30s.

maya: exact. sim details: 200 GPUs, p95 QPS sustained, 3% preemptions/minute burst for 2m every 10m. baseline TPM per-gpu = 1500. aggregate expected RPM ~ 18k. observed effective RPM ~ 16.6k after leak adjustments.

tomas: can you paste the reconciler diff? wondering if faster reconciliation fixes it.

maya: pasted snippet from sim run: ```
# pseudo
for shard in shards:
  ledger = redis.hgetall(shard)
  in_flight = calc_in_flight(ledger)
  tokens_reserved = ledger.tokens - expired_tokens
  if tokens_reserved < 0: tokens_reserved = 0
  // previous reconciler only corrected every 30s
```

jen: short-term mitigation: reduce our token TTL to 3s and run reconcile every 5s for high-risk shards. long-term: idempotent token ops or monotonic counters.

pranav: TTL 3s + 5s reconcile could thrash redis under load tho. any perf numbers?

maya: sim with TTL=3s + reconcile=5s increased redis ops ~1.7x but peak latency still within 95th SLO (120ms) in that sim env. CPU on redis nodes bumped ~15%.

sasha: alternative: local ephemeral lease on node + final flush to redis reduces ops but requires robust crash handling.

tomas: formula we used to estimate effective TPM after leakage: effective_tpm = measured_tpm - leak_rate * active_nodes. leak_rate ~ 0.7 tokens/sec/node in worst-case preemption storms. so: eff_tpm = 1500 - 0.7*1 = 1499.3 per gpu, aggregate gap becomes material at scale.

maya: action items: (1) run a short canary with TTL=3s + 5s reconcile on staging fleet tonight, (2) instrument token-lifecycle traces (span tags: token.status, reconcile.delta), (3) draft a proposal for idempotent token RPC (PR by end of week).

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: eng-infra-staging @ 2026-03-19T02:00Z (duration 1h).

pranav: +1 on traces. also add a fallback admission knob: when redis-latency > 200ms, reduce admitted TPM by 20% to avoid compounding leaks.

jen: note cost tradeoff: faster reconcile increases Redis ops (higher infra cost) but reduces effective token waste and request retries. we should model cost per million tokens vs reconcile freq.

maya: I'll push sim artifacts and cost model to the ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/INFRA-4521. tl;dr: for our workload, paying ~10% extra redis ops avoids ~7% effective TPM loss, net win.

sasha: thanks. if canary looks good, we should backport to Dedicated pools too (they hit similar patterns with eviction windows).

maya: agreed. will update after canary.

pranav: one more ask — include region-breakdown. we saw APAC with higher preemptions -> bigger leak multiplier.

maya: noted, will include per-region leak_rate and propose region-specific admission scales.
